author: Mark Atwood
text:
Public-API design choice — two idiomatic resolutions, both breaking. Pinned to the .18 (inner repr) decision but independently meaningful. Defer to human.

CURRENT SHAPE
- pub fn into_inner(self) -> String — consumes self, yields the hex String.
- impl From<Sha256> for String — same operation via trait. Required by #[serde(into = "String")] adapter.
- Canonical sibling Id newtype (crate-jmap-types/src/id.rs:109) exposes into_inner only, no From<Id> for String.

OPTIONS

(a) Drop into_inner, keep From<Sha256> for String. Callers write String::from(d).
    - Smaller diff.
    - Diverges from the canonical Id template.

(b) Keep into_inner, replace #[serde(into)] with a custom Serialize impl that writes self.0.as_str() directly. Drop From<Sha256> for String.
    - Matches the canonical Id template.
    - Slightly more code (custom Serialize), but the impl is one line: serializer.collect_str(&self.0).
    - The matching custom Deserialize is also wanted under bd:JMAP-sf5h.9.

RECOMMENDATION: (b). The workspace canonical-templates rule favors mirroring Id. Combining this with .9 (custom Deserialize) yields a clean Serialize/Deserialize pair using collect_str + Visitor, eliminating the #[serde(try_from, into)] adapter and the From<Sha256> for String impl that exists only to feed it.

DEPENDENCY ON .18: if .18 picks (B) [u8;32] inner repr, then into_inner -> String becomes a re-encoding helper (not free), changing the calculus. Under (B), the natural shape is into_inner(self) -> [u8; 32] and no From<Sha256> for String at all. The redundancy in .20 collapses by construction under .18=(B), so .20 closes as 'subsumed by .18=(B)'.

Under .18=(A) keep-String, .20 stands and (a) or (b) above is the call.
